nodes.description: A sexually dimorphic female branch has been proposed: SYCP3 variants may perturb meiotic chromosome segregation in oocytes, generating aneuploid oocytes and conceptuses that manifest clinically as recurrent pregnancy loss. In Sycp3-null female mice, chiasma reduction, meiotic chromosome missegregation, oocyte aneuploidy, and early embryo death are well established. In humans the association with recurrent pregnancy loss is contested — reported in a small recurrent-pregnancy-loss cohort but not confirmed in a later study — so this cellular meiotic mechanism is modeled with both supporting and refuting evidence rather than as an established downstream clinical phenotype.

nodes.description: SYCP3 is a structural component of the axial/lateral element of the synaptonemal complex. Loss of functional SYCP3 — through a null allele in mice or a dominant-negative truncating variant in humans — prevents assembly of the axial/lateral elements and of the synaptonemal complex itself, so the scaffold required for homologous-chromosome synapsis fails to form during meiotic prophase I.
